$comment: Design contract: the reason vocabulary of a MailCredential refusal. The names are the ones ADR-0014 section 5.7 allows in a status condition. No reason carries a token, a password, an endpoint that embeds credentials or mailbox content.

reasons.meaning: The credential document declares more than one protocol shape. A credential speaks one protocol, so the request is refused rather than resolved to the first shape that parses.
The credential document uses the legacy shape field. It has no defined semantics and is refused rather than interpreted.
The requested protocol is not in the vocabulary, or the provider or gateway does not serve it. An IMAP endpoint or a JMAP HTTP session never implies an MCP or REST credential.
The referenced target, or one of its parents, does not exist. No default parent is invented and no missing parent is assumed.
A referenced resource lives in another namespace. Every reference is same-namespace, and a Secret stays in the namespace of the credential that owns it.
The capability status of a referenced resource was observed for an older generation. The status describes a resource that no longer exists, so the request fails closed.
A referenced resource or its status could not be read. An unreachable webhook must not silently admit an insecure credential.
The credential asks for Corvi-scoped authority but its provider has no gateway. There are no Corvi-scoped credentials without a gateway.
The credential is bound to a gateway but does not request a nonempty permission list. Gateway scope requires explicit grants.
The credential targets a mailbox while its provider is bound to a gateway. Gateway policy is identity-based.
The bound gateway is suspended or not ready. The credential is never served directly instead.
The provider names a gateway that does not exist. An explicit but invalid gateway reference is not an unbound provider.
The provider cannot issue independently revocable application credentials. Provider administration credentials are never application credentials.
The provider cannot isolate the requested target, so a whole-mailbox token would be handed out under the pretence of identity scope.
A provider-native credential targets an identity whose address is not verified.
A referenced identity, mailbox or provider is suspended.
The requested Secret annotation is not approved by the Secret policy, or is reserved.
A parent resource changed after the credential was issued. The credential has to be authorized again; it is never converted.
The Secret name is taken by another owner, or the Secret changed between the publisher's read and its write. The publisher fails closed instead of clobbering.
A route change has not completed. No two gateways and no direct-provider route serve the same credential authority at the same time.
The published output was withdrawn, but the upstream revocation could not be confirmed. Deleting a Secret is not upstream revocation.
The publisher holds no authorization for the namespace. Admission approval is not publication authorization.
